clue.text: Run down and bring back fish about one

indicators.note: bringing something back sends it the other way, so the built word is read backwards
about means around, so the fish goes round the letter for one

parts.note: an elver is a young eel, a small fish
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Instructions for a trip: go out, come home, and catch a fish on the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts I inside ELVER to make ELIVER, and 'bring back' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: To run someone down is to criticise them harshly, which is to abuse or vilify them.

clue.text: Full eighteen holes consumes some time

indicators.note: consumes means eats, holding the other piece inside

parts.note: eighteen holes make a round of golf

explanation.surface: A golfer's round takes up a fair amount of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' is a link; ROUND swallows T.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotund means plump or rounded, full in figure.

clue.text: Second-hand explosive device has decayed

parts.note: the V-1 was a German flying bomb, with 1 written as I
carious means decayed, said of teeth or bone

explanation.surface: A used bomb that has rotted away.
explanation.walkthrough: The V1 flying bomb gives VI; carious is the dentist's word for decayed.
explanation.definitionFit: Vicarious means experienced through another person, at second hand.

clue.text: Vessel needing reinforcement

definitions.meaning: an inner layer that strengthens or protects

explanation.definitionFit: A liner is an ocean ship and also a strengthening inner lining.

clue.text: On the wrong track one fellow gets lost — as you would expect

indicators.note: something that gets lost goes missing, so these letters are dropped from the phrase

parts.note: to be on the wrong track is to be off course
F is the standard abbreviation for fellow, one letter of it

explanation.surface: A lone man wanders off the trail and goes missing, which is no surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets lost' removes one of the two Fs of OFF COURSE.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning naturally or certainly, just what anyone would expect.

clue.text: Failing? You wouldn't want it to happen on ice

definitions.meaning: a plan that is collapsing is failing to happen

definitions.text: You wouldn't want it to happen on ice
definitions.meaning: a skater would not wish to drop through thin ice

explanation.definitionFit: A deal falling through is failing; literally, a skater breaking the ice drops into the water.

clue.text: Meeting in support of witchcraft curtailed there's a thing!

indicators.note: in a down clue, being in support of means sitting underneath
curtailed means cut short, losing the last letter

parts.note: obi is a form of West Indian sorcery
a session is a meeting

explanation.surface: A coven gathers to back witchcraft but is cut short, which is strange.
explanation.walkthrough: Obi (obeah) is Caribbean witchcraft; 'curtailed' gives OB, with SESSION beneath it in the down entry. 'there's a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a thing about something is to be fixated on it, an obsession.

clue.text: Dust-up resulting in arrest

definitions.meaning: a dust-up is a quarrel or fight
to run someone in is to take them into custody

explanation.definitionFit: A run-in is a squabble; to run in an offender is slang for an arrest.

clue.text: English woman in Scottish isle, where things are most easily seen

definitions.text: where things are most easily seen

indicators.note: in places the woman inside the island

parts.note: Yell is one of the Shetland Islands
Eve was the first woman

explanation.surface: An Englishwoman holidays on a Scottish island with a fine view.
explanation.walkthrough: Yell is in Shetland; EVE goes between its Ls.
explanation.definitionFit: Things at eye level are directly in sight, so they are seen most easily.

clue.text: Decorator's work brings unexpected bonus

definitions.meaning: a cake decorator spreads the icing on top
the phrase means an extra pleasing touch

explanation.definitionFit: Literally the decorator's finishing layer, the idiom means a welcome extra on top of something good.

clue.text: Using specialised skill, catch line when it's thrown

indicators.note: something thrown is tossed about and disordered, so the letters of these words are scrambled

explanation.surface: An angler casts a line with expert skill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when it's' is a link; 'thrown' rearranges the nine letters of CATCH LINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Technical means involving specialist knowledge or expertise, as in a technical skill.

clue.text: Tenor wants experience

definitions.meaning: the tenor of a passage is its gist or meaning
to experience something is to feel or perceive it

explanation.definitionFit: Sense is both the meaning of words and the act of perceiving something.

clue.text: Subtract this as ordered from 19 — it'll form a link

indicators.note: subtract tells us the letters of one word are to be taken away from another
as ordered says the remaining letters are rearranged before comparing

parts.note: 19 across is the phrase meaning to sum up

explanation.surface: An arithmetic instruction: take one thing from clue 19 and get a connection.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of IN SHORT are those of THIS (taken in any order) plus the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nor is a conjunction, a word that links clauses in a sentence.

clue.text: An increase's unusual in a transitional period

indicators.note: unusual signals the letters are put into an odd order

parts.note: increase's is read as increase plus S, the contracted is giving its S

explanation.surface: A remark that a rise in something is out of the ordinary during a period of change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges AN INCREASES; 'in a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Renaissance was the European revival bridging the medieval and modern eras, a transition between periods.

clue.text: Dock owl's tail in error

indicators.note: to dock an animal is to cut off its tail, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: the boobook is a small Australian owl

explanation.surface: A sailor's complaint about a bird whose tail has gone astray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dock' with 'tail' cuts the last letter K from BOOBOOK; a boobook is an Australian owl.
explanation.definitionFit: A booboo is a slang term for a silly mistake or blunder.

clue.text: Paint remover —— brand appears on bottom of box

indicators.note: in a down clue, on the bottom of means placed below

parts.note: a box on the ears is a blow
a brand is a burning stick, a torch

explanation.surface: A trademark is printed on the underside of a carton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appears' is a link; 'box' looks like a container but means hit, and in a down entry 'on bottom of' puts the brand underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: A blowtorch is used to soften old paint so it can be scraped off.

clue.text: I am enthralled by princess and her face

indicators.note: something enthralled by another is held captive inside it

parts.note: Grace Kelly became Princess Grace of Monaco
I am contracts to I'm

explanation.surface: Someone confesses they are captivated by a princess and her looks.
explanation.walkthrough: Princess Grace of Monaco was the film star Grace Kelly; 'and her' merely joins the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A grimace is a twisted expression, and to make a face is to pull one.

clue.text: Stagger endlessly forward with man from South America

indicators.note: endlessly means without its last letter

parts.note: to stagger someone is to amaze them
on means forward, as in moving on
Ian is a man's name

explanation.surface: Someone lurches ahead with a companion from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stagger' looks like a stumble but means astonish.
explanation.definitionFit: Amazonian means of the Amazon region of South America.

clue.text: Problem with skin has grown, spread into lip

indicators.note: into means put inside the other piece

parts.note: the lip of a cup is its rim

indicators.note: spread out means rearranged

explanation.surface: A skin condition has grown and spread to the mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' rearranges GROWN to make NGWOR; 'has' is a link, and 'lip' is the rim of a cup, not the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringworm is a fungal infection causing ring-shaped patches on the skin.

clue.text: To sum up, this month will contain outbreaks of hail or rain

indicators.note: will contain means the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: inst., short for instant, is the old business term for this month

indicators.note: the outbreak of something is its start, so take the first letter of each word

explanation.surface: A weather forecast summary: this month will see scattered hail or rain.
explanation.walkthrough: INST is the old commercial abbreviation for 'this month'; it contains H, O and R.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning briefly or in summary, used to sum up an argument.

clue.text: In a large building exhibit pictures by artist the wrong way round

parts.note: galleries hang pictures to exhibit them

indicators.note: the wrong way round says these letters are written backwards

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: Instructions for showing a painter's work backwards in a big hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a' is a link; RA, a Royal Academician, is the crossword's usual artist, and 'the wrong way round' turns it.
explanation.definitionFit: A hangar is a very large shed for housing aircraft.

clue.text: Engaged in cricket, declare

parts.note: being at work means engaged in it
a Test is an international cricket match

explanation.surface: Playing in a cricket match, a captain declares the innings closed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'declare' looks like the cricket captain ending an innings, but it means state formally.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to declare or bear witness that something is true.

clue.text: Decline to attend race meeting

definitions.meaning: to decline is to deteriorate or go downhill
literally, going to a greyhound race meeting

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to fall into ruin; read literally it is a trip to the greyhound track.

clue.text: Only part of Shakespeare > play that gets the bird over America

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above the next piece

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare play gets booed in America.
explanation.walkthrough: Titus Andronicus is the full title, so the answer is only part of it; to get the bird is to be booed.
explanation.definitionFit: Titus is the first word of the title of Titus Andronicus, Shakespeare's tragedy.

clue.text: Unknown vessel is looming up in the wet

indicators.note: in a down clue, looming up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: Y is an algebraic unknown
SS is a steamship

explanation.surface: A mystery ship rises out of the rain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looming up' reverses YSSIS; 'in the' is a link. 'wet' is the feeble sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Wet in British slang means feeble or weedy, as a sissy is.

clue.text: Plump, overly plump, truthfully, when first seen

indicators.note: only the first letter of each word is seen, so take each initial

explanation.surface: Telling someone frankly that they are rather overweight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plump' looks like a description of a person but is the verb, as in plump for.
explanation.definitionFit: To plump for something is to choose it, which is to opt for it.

clue.text: Cockney more passionate where this carnivore is concerned

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker drops the initial H of a word

parts.note: more passionate means hotter

explanation.surface: A Londoner gets fired up about a meat-eating animal.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney, a working-class Londoner, drops H sounds, so HOTTER loses its H; 'where this ... is concerned' is padding round the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The otter is a fish-eating river mammal belonging to the carnivore order.

clue.text: Clown put home in order that's his milieu

indicators.note: home is put in, placed within the clown

parts.note: an auguste is a type of circus clown with a red nose
in means at home

explanation.surface: A clown tidies up the house, as is his natural element.
explanation.walkthrough: An auguste is a circus clown; IN goes inside it. An Augustine is a friar of the Augustinian order, so the order is his milieu.
explanation.definitionFit: An Augustine friar lives within his religious order, the Augustinians, his natural surroundings.

clue.text: Monkey —- mice —- fish snake --…

indicators.note: to snake is to wind about, so the letters twist into a new order

explanation.surface: A list of creatures, like a children's game of animals.
explanation.walkthrough: Monkey here is a mischievous child, or mischief itself; 'snake' as a verb rearranges MICE and FISH.
explanation.definitionFit: To monkey about is to cause trouble, and monkey business is playful naughtiness.

clue.text: 9 … bird — seal —- if you just listen!

indicators.note: just listening means taking the sound and not the spelling

parts.note: a signet is a small seal, as on a ring

explanation.surface: The list of animals goes on, adding a bird and a seal.
explanation.walkthrough: Continues the list from 28; the signet seal is heard as the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A cygnet is a young swan, a bird.
